basis.governing_question: Should Quinta Azul enter the retail markets of Spain, France, Germany and Poland, and in which order?

sub_questions.question: How attractive is each of the four retail markets for Quinta Azul's olive oil?
Can Quinta Azul win against competitors in each market, and which capability gaps stand in the way?
Which entry option fits each market, and what does its business case show?
Is each of the four countries a go or a no-go?
In what order, and with what entry plan, should the countries that are a go be entered?

drivers.evidence: the retail markets of Spain, France, Germany and Poland

work.unit: Market assessed in full (demand, channels, competitors, regulation, buyer interviews)

phase_work.why: Four markets screened at once, then three assessed in full two at a time; the second batch can run past the usual 8 weeks.

work.unit: Entry option and business case for one market
Entry sequence and roadmap across markets

phase_work.why: Business cases for three markets, two at a time, then the sequence and roadmap; the top runs a week past the usual 6.

sizing.levers: A shortlist of two markets instead of three would shorten Research by 2 to 3 weeks and Design by 1 to 2.

phases.name: Research
phases.objective_one_line: Assess demand, competition and Quinta Azul's capability to win in each of the four retail markets.

gate.label: Go/no-go on Design
gate.decision: Which of the four markets go forward into entry-option design?

phases.name: Design
phases.objective_one_line: Define the entry options, go or no-go per market, and the entry plan and sequence.

gate.label: Final decision
gate.decision: Approve the go or no-go for each market and the entry sequence?

architect_notes: Engagement length is not given; 11 to 15 weeks is an estimate from the work, and every piece running long would reach 17.
Plan assumes three of the four markets reach full assessment after the desk screen; a shortlist of two would cut 3 to 5 weeks.
